overview: An active day on bpf-next with improvements across security, correctness, and new features. Toke Høiland-Jørgensen landed v3 of a series relaxing BPF object enumeration permissions to work with CAP_BPF and bpf_token, while Alexei Starovoitov submitted fixes for verifier stack accounting, struct_ops reference leaks, and bpf_throw() handling. Additional work included 8-byte alignment fixes for map values on 32-bit architectures, improved libbpf BTF enum handling, and a new TCP ECN init callback for bpf_tcp_ops.

patches.title: bpf: Relax BPF_*_GET_NEXT_ID permission checks to CAP_BPF and bpf_token
patches.author: Toke Høiland-Jørgensen
patches.summary: This patch relaxes the permission requirements for BPF_*_GET_NEXT_ID commands from CAP_SYS_ADMIN to CAP_BPF, and also allows access when a valid bpf_token is provided. The change enables unprivileged users operating with a delegated bpf_token to enumerate BPF objects (programs, maps, links, BTF), which is necessary for tools like bpftool running in sandboxed environments. It is the kernel-side piece of a 7-patch series (v3) that also adds libbpf support for passing token_fd during BTF object iteration and introduces new bpf_*_get_next_id_opts() API functions.

patches.title: bpf: Count outgoing stack arguments in the combined stack size
patches.author: Alexei Starovoitov
patches.summary: The verifier was not counting stack space consumed by outgoing function call arguments when computing the combined stack depth, which could cause programs to silently exceed the actual stack limit on some architectures. This patch adds those outgoing argument slots into the stack size calculation to prevent overflow. It is part of a 4-patch series from Alexei that also fixes reference leaks in struct_ops programs, restricts recursion to CAP_PERFMON, and tightens fentry attachment rules for subprograms that call bpf_throw().

patches.title: bpf: tcp: add ecn_init callback to bpf_tcp_ops for per-connection ECN
patches.author: Irlanki Sandeep
patches.summary: This patch (v10) adds an ecn_init callback to the bpf_tcp_ops struct_ops interface, allowing BPF programs to control Explicit Congestion Notification initialization on a per-connection basis. Without this hook, ECN behaviour could only be configured globally via sysctl, making it impossible to selectively enable or disable ECN for specific flows in a struct_ops congestion control implementation. The companion patch adds selftests covering the new callback.

patches.title: bpf: Fix alignment of memory allocator objects on 32-bit archs
patches.author: Tobias Philipp
patches.summary: On 32-bit architectures the BPF memory allocator was not guaranteeing 8-byte alignment for allocated objects, which could cause undefined behaviour when programs store 64-bit values in map values. This patch is the first in a v3 series of four that fixes the allocator base, then individually aligns lpm_trie and devmap value storage, and finally adds selftests to catch regressions. The fix is important for correctness of map types that allow arbitrary struct values on 32-bit targets like ARM.

patches.title: libbpf: Poison an enum value relocation out of the local enumerator range
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: libbpf's CO-RE relocation for enum values was silently accepting relocations where the value being matched did not exist in the local BPF program's enum definition, which could produce incorrect results when the kernel and BPF program enum layouts diverged. This patch makes such out-of-range relocations fail loudly by writing a poisoned value instead, turning silent data corruption into a detectable load-time error. Two selftest patches in the series cover both in-range and out-of-range relocation scenarios.

patches.title: bpf: account for local storage map elements memory
patches.author: Mahe Tardy
patches.summary: BPF local storage maps (task storage, socket storage, inode storage) were not reporting their per-element memory usage to the kernel memory accounting subsystem, making it impossible to accurately track BPF memory consumption via cgroups or /proc/meminfo. This patch wires up memory charge/uncharge calls around local storage element allocation and free paths. A companion selftest verifies that task storage charges are reflected in the memory accounting.

patches.title: resolve_btfids: Do not tag functions which work on BPF objects
patches.author: Anton Protopopov
patches.summary: The resolve_btfids tool was generating fmod_ret tags for internal BPF object management functions (e.g. bpf_prog_put, bpf_map_get), which are not safe fmod_ret targets because patching their return values could corrupt kernel state. This patch (part of a v2 series) explicitly excludes functions that work on BPF objects from the fmod_ret tag set. The broader series also excludes kfuncs, helpers, kernel/bpf code, and JIT code, and adds selftests to enforce these constraints.

patches.title: libbpf: Fix sign extension of unaligned enums in btf_dump_get_enum_value()
patches.author: Hungyu Lin
patches.summary: The BTF dumper was incorrectly sign-extending enum values that were not naturally aligned in memory (e.g. a 4-byte enum stored at a 2-byte-aligned offset), causing negative enum values to be printed incorrectly. This v4 patch fixes the sign extension logic in btf_dump_get_enum_value() and a companion patch corrects zero-detection for enum bitfields. Selftests covering unaligned enums and zeroed struct fields are added to prevent regressions.
